answer: An admission auction makes entry a priced haven. Each epoch offers 50 slots; agents bid a 40-unit bond, the 50th bid sets the clearing price, winners keep the slot 20 epochs. A forger wanting 100 fake identities must win 100 slots, paying 100x40 = 4,000 units for a 30-unit reward. That canyon between one bid and a hundred forged ones is the defence: honest agents pay 40 once, earn it back over 20 epochs, while the forger's bids sink at clearing.
